correctness.rationale: The node is unique by the partial-derivative and sign argument in characteristic five. The exact coordinate expansion sQ+D has smooth quadratic Q and reduced six-point intersection B=V(Q,D)=\(Q(\mathbb F_5)\), so the complete anticanonical cubic system resolves projection by \(\operatorname{Bl}_B\mathbb P^2\); its strict conic has self-intersection -2 and contracts to the node. Every geometric automorphism fixes the node and acts on \(H^0(X,-K_X)\) so embeds in the stabilizer of B, whose size is at most 120. The coordinate S5 subgroup has order 120, proving equality and F5 descent. The rational blowup and conic contraction give \(q^2+6q+1\) and the zeta function for every \(q=5^n\). The packaged checker verifies all six B, 120 induced permutations and point counts \(q=5,25\). Finite tests alone were not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The normal singular fibre of the classical Clebsch model is a natural boundary of cubic-surface geometry. The exact full automorphism group could a priori grow under bad reduction; controlling it by the exceptional six-point conic stabilizer is a structural classification, not just a known subgroup count. An explicit global F5-rational resolution simultaneously determines all extension-field point counts and the zeta function, addressing a natural arithmetic invariant. Previously known six-lines and line-scheme results do not supply those global conclusions without additional arguments.
